palette.notes: Uses the 32-colour UFO 50 palette; notes that 16 and 32 colours are common choices. Advises picking an existing palette rather than theorising; the orc ends with three shades of green on its skin.

lighting: One light source above and slightly in front of the sprite: tops and fronts bright, shades added to bottom and back. Check by removing saturation to see if shading still reads.
silhouette: Squint test: large clusters of light and dark should read through details. At 32x32, colour shapes define the sprite more than outlines (Mario has no outline); chibi proportions buy expression.

motion.timing: Static sprite tutorial; no animation timing.

texture: Sparing dithering, mostly for rough surfaces or large flat areas; shading done with unbroken clusters. Anti-aliasing smooths inner curves only.
camera: None; single sprite placed in a game screenshot for scale (96x96 is large next to a 384x224 screen).

acting.acts: No acting; the lesson for staging is scale: a 96x96 sprite fills an arcade screen, a 32x32 one must lean on head size and colour.

techniques: single light from above-front; shade bottom and back
clean one-pixel lines with few jaggies
anti-alias inner corners only, never the outside edge
selective outline: light colours where light hits, shadow colours for inner segmentation
sketch small sprites with colour shapes, not outlines
chibi proportions for small expressive characters
flip horizontally and desaturate to check form
dither sparingly; save as PNG/GIF, never JPG
feel: one top-front light + selout instead of black lines + chunky clusters = solid, clean sprite that reads when squinting
for_fred: Give Fred and Pixie selective outlines: dark only on the shadow side and under the body, light or none on top, and never anti-alias their outer edge since the reel background changes. Keep their heads big (chibi) so faces read at TikTok scale, and run the desaturate test on every new pose.
